question: The chemical name of baking soda is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chemical name of baking soda is **sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3)**, also commonly known as bicarbonate of soda.
 
• Baking soda is a white crystalline solid but often appears as a fine powder.
 
• It is widely used as a leavening agent in cooking, especially in baking, where it reacts with acidic components to release carbon dioxide gas, causing the dough to rise.
 
• It is mildly alkaline and can neutralize acids, which is why it is used for relieving indigestion and as a cleaning agent.
 
• Baking soda decomposes at high temperatures to form sodium carbonate (Na2CO3), water (H2O), and carbon dioxide (CO2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leavening Agent:**

 
 
• Baking soda acts as a leavening agent in baked goods by reacting with acids like vinegar, yogurt, or lemon juice to release carbon dioxide gas.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:**
 
 
• It neutralizes acidic substances, making it useful in antacids for relieving heartburn and indigestion.
 
 
 
• **Cleaning Agent:**
 
 
• Baking soda is commonly used as a household cleaning agent due to its ability to dissolve dirt and grease.
 
• It is also used to deodorize refrigerators and carpets.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition of Baking Soda:**
 
 
• When heated, sodium hydrogen carbonate decomposes into sodium carbonate, water, and carbon dioxide, which is why it is used in fire extinguishers.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Baking Powder:**
 
 
• Baking powder contains sodium hydrogen carbonate and an acidic component, allowing it to work without additional acids, unlike baking soda.
